A common path is: relevant associate or bachelor's degree -> obtain a CTE teaching credential -> enter a vocational college, technical institute, or community college -> teach occupational courses and practical training -> participate in skills and teaching competitions -> advance in professional title, lead a team, or move into academic administration.

This work suits people who understand technology and want to teach. If you explain complex principles plainly and patiently correct students' hand movements at the training bench, the occupation can be a strong fit.

Career/Technical Education Teachers, Postsecondary teach occupational skills at community colleges, vocational colleges, technical institutes, and related postsecondary institutions. They teach practical subjects such as automotive repair, electrical work, nursing, and computing, organize hands-on training, and guide students into employment.

The occupation's greatest risk is not AI but enrollment and funding. Vocational-college enrollment and appropriations depend heavily on policy, while programs follow industry change. A popular automotive program today can require a shift toward new energy within a few years, creating constant curriculum-update pressure.
